description: Fetch a project by `project_reference` from the self-host store. Optional `version_reference` pins to a specific version of that project (a version from another project is a tool error); otherwise the latest live (published or approved) version is used, or the latest non-archived version of any status if none is live. Returns `{ project_reference, version_reference, version, name, description, status, summary, created_at, updated_at, project_url, version_url, latest_draft, clipped_collections, documents, next_steps, model }`. `documents` lists the indexed project documents that apply to this version (`[{ document_reference, title, pages }]`) — search them with search_docs. The model is a summary for reading, never a file to hand back. Every `collection` step is stamped with `__context` (`total_rows`, `shown_rows`, `columns`, `shape`, `truncated`, `patchable`; an empty table gets `total_rows: 0`, `columns: []`, `patchable: true`): tables of up to 100 rows are shown whole and can be changed with patch_version; bigger ones are clipped, listed in `clipped_collections`, and can only change by the user downloading the model from `version_url`, you amending it, and the user uploading it. `latest_draft` is the newest draft version (null if none) — patches go there, so call get_project again with its version_reference before patching. Follow `next_steps` and tell the user which route applies before making changes. All other model content — input.format, steps, expressions, output — is returned verbatim so an LLM caller can understand what the project does and how to build a valid input payload. Precursor to run_quote and patch_version.

project_reference.description: UUID of the project to fetch.

version_reference.description: Optional. Specific version UUID of this project; defaults to the latest live version, or the latest non-archived version of any status if none are live.
